experiences.name: Prague Castle Complex Exploration
experiences.description: Spend a half-day exploring the largest ancient castle complex in the world, including St. Vitus Cathedral, the Old Royal Palace, and Golden Lane. Wander through centuries of Bohemian history with stunning panoramic views over the red-roofed city below.

experiences.name: Budapest Thermal Bath Experience at Széchenyi
experiences.description: Soak in one of Europe's largest and most iconic thermal bath complexes, built in 1913 in stunning Neo-Baroque style. Enjoy indoor and outdoor pools fed by natural hot springs, a deeply rooted Hungarian cultural tradition dating back to Ottoman rule.

experiences.name: Old Town Prague & Charles Bridge Walking Tour
experiences.description: Join a guided walking tour through Prague's UNESCO-listed Old Town, crossing the iconic 14th-century Charles Bridge adorned with 30 Baroque statues. Discover the Astronomical Clock, Týn Church, and hidden medieval courtyards with rich storytelling from a local guide.

experiences.name: Buda Castle Hill & Hungarian National History Museum
experiences.description: Explore the historic Buda Castle district, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, including the Hungarian National Museum housed within the castle. Walk Fisherman's Bastion for sweeping views of the Danube and Parliament, and discover the layered history from medieval kings to Habsburg rule.

experiences.name: Czech & Hungarian Street Food & Market Crawl
experiences.description: Embark on a self-guided food crawl starting at Prague's Manifesto Market and ending in Budapest's Great Market Hall. Sample trdelník pastries, svíčková beef, chimney cakes, lángos fried bread, and Hungarian goulash — a delicious deep dive into Central European culinary heritage.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Eastern Europe (Prague + Budapest)
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Václav Havel Airport Prague at 22:30. Clear customs, collect luggage, and take the budget-friendly Airport Express bus (Line AE) to Prague city centre (~60 CZK). Check in to your accommodation, freshen up, and grab a late-night snack near the hostel area.

meals.breakfast: N/A – In flight
meals.lunch: N/A – In flight
meals.dinner: Late-night kebab or open-faced sandwich (chlebíček) from a 24-hour convenience store or late-night street food stall near accommodation (~80–120 CZK)

day_by_day.notes: Keep energy light on arrival night. Buy a 3-day Prague public transport pass the next morning to save money. Exchange a small amount of currency at the airport (avoid airport exchange booths with bad rates – use an ATM instead). Budget tip: Avoid taxis; use bus Line 119 + Metro or the Airport Express bus.

day_by_day.morning: Start the day with a walk across the iconic Charles Bridge at sunrise (free) – fewer crowds and beautiful golden light on the statues. Stroll into the Lesser Town (Malá Strana) and admire the baroque architecture. Head up to Prague Castle (Hradčany) – explore the castle grounds and St. Vitus Cathedral exterior for free; optional paid entry to interior (~250 CZK for short circuit ticket).
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend through Nerudova Street into Lesser Town. Cross back over Charles Bridge and explore Old Town (Staré Město). Visit the Old Town Square and watch the famous Astronomical Clock (Orloj) chime on the hour – free to watch from outside. Browse the square and surrounding medieval lanes.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Jewish Quarter (Josefov) from the outside (free to walk through). Head to Wenceslas Square for an evening stroll. Enjoy a budget Czech dinner at a local pub (pivnice).

meals.breakfast: Grab a fresh pastry (koláč) and coffee at a local bakery near Old Town (~60–80 CZK)
meals.lunch: Budget Czech lunch at a local canteen (jídelna) – try svíčková (beef sirloin with cream sauce) or goulash with bread dumplings (~150–200 CZK)
meals.dinner: Traditional Czech pub dinner – pork knee (vepřové koleno) or fried cheese (smažený sýr) with a half-litre of Czech beer at a local pivnice (~200–280 CZK)

day_by_day.notes: Prague Castle is best visited early to avoid crowds. The castle grounds are free to enter; only interior buildings require tickets. Wear comfortable walking shoes – cobblestones throughout Old Town and Castle District. Budget tip: Tap water is safe and free to refill bottles.

day_by_day.morning: Take the metro to Vinohrady neighbourhood – a charming, less-touristy residential district. Visit the Church of St. Ludmila (free exterior, small fee inside). Walk through Náměstí Míru (Peace Square) and explore the art nouveau architecture of the area. Head to Vyšehrad Fortress (free entry to grounds) for panoramic views of Prague and the Vltava River.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Vyšehrad Cemetery (free) – resting place of famous Czechs including Dvořák and Smetana. Walk along the Vltava riverbank back toward the city centre. Visit the Náplavka riverside embankment – a lively promenade with local market stalls (especially active on weekends). Cross to the Smíchov side for a quieter local experience.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Letná Park area for sunset views over Prague's rooftops and the river from the Letná Beer Garden (one of the cheapest beers in Prague, ~40–55 CZK per half-litre). Enjoy the view and local atmosphere before heading back to rest.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hostel or a local café – yogurt, toast, and coffee (~80–100 CZK)
meals.lunch: Street food at Náplavka market or a nearby takeaway – try trdelník (chimney cake) as a snack, plus a sandwich (~100–150 CZK)
meals.dinner: Budget dinner at a Vinohrady neighbourhood restaurant – pasta, pizza, or Czech daily special (denní menu) which includes soup + main (~180–220 CZK)

day_by_day.notes: Vyšehrad is an underrated gem and far less crowded than Prague Castle. The Letná Beer Garden is cash only and extremely popular with locals – a great authentic experience. September weather in Prague is mild (15–22°C) – bring a light jacket for evenings.

day_by_day.morning: Morning free to revisit any favourite spots or explore the Žižkov neighbourhood – known for its quirky Žižkov Television Tower (exterior free; observation deck ~180 CZK) with famous crawling baby sculptures by David Černý. Walk through this bohemian, artsy district.
day_by_day.afternoon: Pack your bag and check out of Prague accommodation. Take a budget bus or train to Budapest. Recommended: FlixBus or RegioJet from Prague to Budapest (~6–8 hours, book in advance for ~15–30 EUR). Alternatively, take a scenic train (~7 hours, ~25–40 EUR). Depart early-mid afternoon to arrive in Budapest by evening.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in Budapest (Keleti or Népliget station). Take the metro or tram to your accommodation area. Check in, freshen up, and take a short evening stroll along the Danube riverbank to see the illuminated Parliament building and Chain Bridge – one of Europe's most stunning night views (free).

meals.breakfast: Grab a quick breakfast before checkout – hostel breakfast or local bakery (~80–100 CZK)
meals.lunch: Pack snacks for the bus/train journey – grab items from a supermarket (Lidl/Billa) before departure (~100–150 CZK / ~400–600 HUF)
meals.dinner: First taste of Budapest – try a lángos (deep-fried flatbread with sour cream and cheese) from a street vendor near the river (~800–1,200 HUF)

day_by_day.notes: Book your Prague–Budapest bus/train ticket at least a few days in advance for the best budget prices. FlixBus is often the cheapest option. Upon arrival in Budapest, buy a 72-hour or 96-hour public transport pass (BKK) to cover metro, trams, and buses (~5,500–7,200 HUF). Budapest uses Hungarian Forint (HUF) – use ATMs for the best rates.

day_by_day.morning: Start with Buda Castle Hill – take the funicular (Sikló) up (~1,400 HUF one way) or hike up the stairs for free. Explore Buda Castle (exterior free; museum entry optional ~2,800 HUF), Matthias Church (entry ~2,000 HUF), and the stunning Fisherman's Bastion (free for most areas, small fee for upper terraces). Panoramic views over the Danube and Pest side.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk down to the Chain Bridge (Széchenyi Lánchíd) and cross on foot into Pest – free and iconic. Explore the grand Andrássy Avenue (a UNESCO World Heritage boulevard). Visit Heroes' Square (Hősök tere) – completely free and architecturally magnificent. Stroll through City Park (Városliget) – free green space with Vajdahunyad Castle (free exterior).
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Great Market Hall (Nagycsarnok) if still open (closes ~18:00 on Saturdays) – browse local produce, paprika, and souvenirs. Walk along the Danube Promenade (Duna-korzó) at dusk for stunning views of the illuminated Buda side. Enjoy a ruin bar experience at Szimpla Kert – Budapest's most famous ruin bar in the Jewish Quarter.

meals.breakfast: Hungarian breakfast at a local café – fresh bread, butter, jam, and coffee (~1,200–1,500 HUF)
meals.lunch: Lunch at a local étterem (restaurant) – try gulyás (goulash soup) with bread (~2,000–2,800 HUF)
meals.dinner: Budget dinner in the Jewish Quarter (VII district) – falafel, kebab, or Hungarian street food (~1,500–2,200 HUF); drinks at Szimpla Kert (~800–1,200 HUF per beer)

day_by_day.notes: Saturday is market day at the Great Market Hall – arrive before 17:00. The Jewish Quarter (Erzsébetváros) is Budapest's nightlife and cultural hub – very walkable. Ruin bars are a unique Budapest experience – Szimpla Kert is the original and most atmospheric. Budget tip: Many museums in Budapest are free for EU citizens under 26.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Hungarian Parliament Building (Országház) – one of the world's most beautiful parliament buildings. Book a guided interior tour in advance (~6,000 HUF for non-EU visitors; free for EU citizens). Admire the exterior and the Danube embankment. Walk to the Shoes on the Danube Bank memorial – a moving Holocaust memorial (free).
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross the river to Buda and visit Gellért Hill – hike up for free (about 20–30 minutes) to the Citadella and Liberty Statue for the best panoramic views of Budapest. Descend and visit the Gellért Thermal Baths area (exterior free; bathing entry ~7,000–9,000 HUF – optional but highly recommended as a Budapest cultural experience).
day_by_day.evening: Explore the historic Óbuda district (the oldest part of Budapest) or return to the Pest side. Visit St. Stephen's Basilica (free exterior; small donation for interior; tower entry ~800 HUF for city views). Evening stroll along Váci Street (main pedestrian shopping street) and grab dinner in the VIII or IX district for more local, less touristy prices.

meals.breakfast: Sunday market breakfast or hostel breakfast – fresh pastry (rétes/strudel) and coffee (~1,000–1,400 HUF)
meals.lunch: Affordable lunch near Gellért Hill – try a local étterem daily menu (napi menü) with soup + main (~2,200–3,000 HUF)
meals.dinner: Traditional Hungarian dinner – chicken paprikash (paprikás csirke) with nokedli dumplings at a local restaurant in the VIII district (~2,500–3,500 HUF)

day_by_day.notes: Parliament tours must be booked online in advance at the official website – slots fill up fast, especially on weekends. Gellért Baths is pricier but a once-in-a-lifetime cultural experience – budget for it if possible. Sunday in Budapest is quieter and lovely for walking. The Danube is most beautiful at golden hour from Gellért Hill.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Hungarian National Museum (Nemzeti Múzeum) – excellent history exhibits covering Hungary from prehistoric times to the present (~1,600 HUF entry; free on some days). Explore the nearby Múzeum Boulevard area. Head to the Central Market area and explore the IX district (Ferencváros) – an up-and-coming cultural neighbourhood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the metro to Városliget (City Park) and visit the Széchenyi Thermal Baths – the largest medicinal bath complex in Europe and a Budapest institution (~6,500–8,000 HUF entry). Soak in the outdoor and indoor pools – a relaxing and affordable afternoon. Alternatively, visit the Budapest Zoo (adjacent, ~4,500 HUF) or the Museum of Fine Arts (free on certain days).
day_by_day.evening: Return to the city centre and explore the Gozsdu Udvar (Gozsdu Courtyard) in the Jewish Quarter – a series of interconnected courtyards lined with bars, restaurants, and street food stalls. Perfect for a budget evening of food and drinks. Catch live music if available at local venues.

meals.breakfast: Local bakery breakfast – fresh kifli (crescent roll) with butter and coffee (~800–1,200 HUF)
meals.lunch: Quick lunch near the museum or park – lángos or a sandwich from a local büfé (~1,000–1,500 HUF)
meals.dinner: Street food dinner at Gozsdu Udvar – burgers, tacos, or Hungarian bites with a craft beer (~2,000–3,000 HUF total)

day_by_day.notes: Széchenyi Baths is a must-do in Budapest – bring a swimsuit, towel, and flip-flops (or rent on-site for extra cost). Weekday afternoons are less crowded than weekends. Budget tip: Buy thermal bath entry online in advance for small discounts. The Gozsdu Courtyard is free to enter and great for budget grazing – order small plates from multiple vendors.

day_by_day.morning: Last morning in Budapest – revisit a favourite spot or explore a neighbourhood you missed. Consider the Dohány Street Synagogue (Nagy Zsinagóga) – the largest synagogue in Europe and second largest in the world (~5,000 HUF entry; includes the Jewish Museum and memorial garden). A deeply moving and architecturally stunning site.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final souvenir shopping at the Great Market Hall or local shops – pick up Hungarian paprika, pálinka (fruit brandy), and handmade crafts. Enjoy a leisurely coffee at a classic Budapest café (kávéház). Begin making your way to Budapest Liszt Ferenc International Airport (BUD) – take the 100E airport bus from Deák Ferenc tér (~900 HUF, no transfer needed).
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Budapest. Reflect on an incredible 8-day journey through two of Central Europe's most beautiful and historic cities – Prague and Budapest – rich in culture, history, and unforgettable experiences.

meals.breakfast: Final Hungarian breakfast – langos or a full breakfast at a local café (~1,200–1,800 HUF)
meals.lunch: Farewell lunch at a traditional Hungarian restaurant – try töltött káposzta (stuffed cabbage) or halászlé (fisherman's soup) (~2,500–3,500 HUF)
meals.dinner: Airport meal or light snack before departure – grab a sandwich or snack from a shop (~1,500–2,000 HUF)

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for airport travel and security. The 100E airport bus runs frequently and is the most budget-friendly airport transfer option. Final budget summary tip: This 8-day trip can comfortably be done for approximately €50–70/day (including accommodation, food, transport, and entry fees) if you plan ahead, use public transport, eat at local restaurants, and take advantage of free attractions. Prague tends to be slightly cheaper than Budapest for food; both cities are excellent value compared to Western Europe.

trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight UA arrives at 22:30. No morning or afternoon activities scheduled.
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – In transit.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Václav Havel Airport Prague at 22:30. Clear customs, collect luggage, and transfer to your accommodation in Prague (approximately 30–40 minutes by taxi or airport express bus). Check in, freshen up, and get a good night's rest. If hungry, grab a light snack from the hotel or a nearby 24-hour convenience store.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport before departure
meals.lunch: On the plane or at a transit airport
meals.dinner: Light snack at the hotel or nearby convenience store upon arrival – budget ~€5–10

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light. Pre-book your airport transfer in advance to avoid long taxi queues late at night. Have Czech koruna (CZK) or a card ready for the transfer. The Aegean Bliss Resort is your Prague base – confirm check-in details with the hotel ahead of arrival.

day_by_day.morning: Start with a leisurely breakfast at the hotel, then head to Prague Old Town (Staré Město). Explore the iconic Old Town Square, admire the Astronomical Clock (Orloj) and watch the hourly show, and wander through the medieval lanes. Visit the Church of Our Lady before Týn for a stunning Gothic façade.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross the legendary Charles Bridge (Karlův most), pausing to admire the Baroque statues and panoramic views of the Vltava River. Continue uphill to Prague Castle (Pražský hrad) – explore St. Vitus Cathedral, the Old Royal Palace, and Golden Lane. Allow 2–3 hours for the castle complex.
day_by_day.evening: Descend from the castle into the Malá Strana (Lesser Town) neighborhood. Stroll through charming cobblestone streets and enjoy dinner at a traditional Czech restaurant. Try svíčková (beef sirloin with cream sauce) or svíčková with knedlíky (bread dumplings). End the evening with a walk along the illuminated Charles Bridge.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a nearby café – try a fresh pastry and coffee (~€6–10)
meals.lunch: Casual lunch near Old Town Square – try a local Czech bistro for goulash soup and bread (~€10–14)
meals.dinner: Traditional Czech restaurant in Malá Strana – budget ~€18–25 per person including a local Pilsner Urquell beer

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes – this is a very walkable day covering significant ground. Prague Castle is one of the largest castle complexes in the world; arrive early afternoon to avoid peak crowds. Purchase a combined castle ticket (~€14) for access to multiple buildings.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Jewish Quarter (Josefov), one of the best-preserved Jewish historic districts in Europe. Tour the Old Jewish Cemetery, the Old-New Synagogue (Europe's oldest active synagogue), and the Pinkas Synagogue with its haunting Holocaust memorial. Allow 2 hours for the quarter.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Wenceslas Square (Václavské náměstí) in the New Town – a grand boulevard lined with shops, cafés, and historic buildings. Visit the National Museum at the top of the square. Then explore Vinohrady neighborhood for a taste of local Prague life, away from tourist crowds. Pop into a local kavárna (café) for a mid-afternoon coffee break.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a classical music concert or opera performance – Prague is renowned for its vibrant music scene. Many churches and historic venues host evening concerts (tickets ~€15–30). Afterward, enjoy dinner in the Vinohrady or Žižkov district at a modern Czech bistro.

meals.breakfast: Café breakfast near the hotel – avocado toast or eggs and coffee (~€8–12)
meals.lunch: Light lunch near Josefov – try a soup and sandwich at a local deli (~€9–13)
meals.dinner: Modern Czech bistro in Vinohrady – try duck confit or roasted pork with red cabbage (~€18–24)

day_by_day.notes: The Jewish Quarter combined ticket costs approximately €16–20 and covers six sites – well worth it. Book concert tickets in advance online, especially for popular venues like the Municipal House (Obecní dům) or St. James Basilica.

day_by_day.morning: Take a half-day trip to Vyšehrad, Prague's second castle and a peaceful hilltop fortress with panoramic city views. Explore the Vyšehrad Cemetery (resting place of Czech luminaries including Dvořák and Mucha), the Basilica of St. Peter and St. Paul, and the ancient Romanesque rotunda. Far fewer crowds than Prague Castle.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the city center and visit the Mucha Museum, dedicated to the Art Nouveau master Alfons Mucha – a compact but fascinating collection (~€13 entry). Afterward, browse the local shops and markets in the Nové Město area. Visit the Náměstí Míru square in Vinohrady for local atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a farewell dinner in Prague at a rooftop restaurant or riverside terrace with views of the Vltava. This is your last evening in Prague before heading to Budapest tomorrow. Pack your bags tonight and confirm your morning travel arrangements.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a bakery near the hotel – fresh croissant and coffee (~€6–9)
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch near Vyšehrad – pick up supplies from a local grocery or deli (~€8–12)
meals.dinner: Rooftop or riverside restaurant in Prague – splurge slightly for a memorable farewell meal (~€22–30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Vyšehrad is reachable by metro (Line C, Vyšehrad station) in about 15 minutes from the city center. Tonight, prepare for the journey to Budapest tomorrow – the most popular option is the Regiojet or FlixBus overnight train/bus (~€20–40) or a morning train via RegioJet (~4.5 hours). Book in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day from Prague to Budapest. Take the morning train or bus (depart ~08:00–09:00, arrive Budapest ~13:00–14:00). Enjoy the scenic Central European countryside en route. Upon arrival at Budapest Keleti or Kelenföld station, transfer to your accommodation and check in.
day_by_day.afternoon: After settling in, take a gentle orientation walk along the Danube Promenade (Duna-korzó) on the Pest side. Admire views of Buda Castle and the Chain Bridge. Visit the iconic Hungarian Parliament Building exterior – one of Europe's most beautiful Neo-Gothic buildings. Stroll through Vörösmarty Square.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Great Market Hall (Nagyvásárcsarnok) if still open (closes ~18:00 on Saturdays) for local produce, Hungarian paprika, and souvenirs. Then head to the vibrant ruin bar district in the Jewish Quarter (VII district) – start your Budapest evenings at Szimpla Kert, the original ruin bar, for a local craft beer or pálinka (Hungarian fruit brandy).

meals.breakfast: Grab a pastry and coffee at Prague station before boarding (~€5–8)
meals.lunch: Snack on the train or grab a quick bite near Budapest station upon arrival (~€8–12)
meals.dinner: Traditional Hungarian restaurant near the ruin bar district – try goulash (gulyás), chicken paprikash, or lángos (~€16–22 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book your Prague–Budapest train ticket in advance via the Czech Railways (CD) or RegioJet website. A direct train takes approximately 6–7 hours; the RegioJus bus is ~7 hours but cheaper. Budapest uses Hungarian Forint (HUF) – withdraw cash or use a card widely accepted in restaurants and hotels.

day_by_day.morning: Cross the Chain Bridge to the Buda side and hike or take the funicular up to Buda Castle (Budavári Palota). Explore the Hungarian National Gallery inside the castle for free or a small fee, and enjoy sweeping panoramic views over the Danube and Pest. Walk through the charming Castle District (Várnegyed) and visit Matthias Church and the Fisherman's Bastion – a fairytale Neo-Romanesque terrace with spectacular river views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend to the Buda side and visit the Gellért Hill (Gellért-hegy) – a 30-minute uphill walk rewarded with arguably the best panoramic view in Budapest. See the Liberty Statue at the top. Afterward, treat yourself to a visit to the famous Gellért Thermal Baths, one of Budapest's most ornate Art Nouveau bathhouses (entry ~€25–30 including locker).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Pest via the Liberty Bridge (Szabadság híd). Enjoy dinner in the lively Ráday Street restaurant corridor or in the Palace Quarter (VIII district). End the evening with a leisurely walk along the illuminated Danube embankment – a UNESCO World Heritage Site at night.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a local Hungarian bakery (pékség) – try a fresh kifli (crescent roll) with butter and coffee (~€5–8)
meals.lunch: Casual lunch in the Castle District – a Hungarian bistro serving stuffed peppers or bean soup (~€12–16)
meals.dinner: Sit-down dinner in Ráday Street – try beef pörkölt (Hungarian stew) or töltött káposzta (stuffed cabbage) (~€17–23 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Fisherman's Bastion has free access to the outer terraces; the upper tower has a small entry fee (~€3). Book Gellért Baths online in advance on weekends to secure a time slot. Wear comfortable shoes for the Gellért Hill climb – the path is paved but steep.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Hungarian Parliament Building – book a guided interior tour in advance (~€20 for non-EU citizens). The interior is breathtaking, featuring the Hungarian Holy Crown and stunning Neo-Gothic architecture. Afterward, explore the nearby Kossuth Square and the Ethnography Museum opposite the Parliament.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Jewish Quarter (VII district) – visit the Great Synagogue on Dohány Street (Dohány utcai zsinagóga), the largest synagogue in Europe (~€15 entry including museum). Walk through the Hungarian Jewish Museum and the Raoul Wallenberg Memorial Park. Then browse the eclectic shops and street art of the ruin district by day.
day_by_day.evening: Take an evening cruise on the Danube River – a 1-hour sightseeing cruise (~€15–20) offers magical views of the illuminated Parliament, Chain Bridge, and Buda Castle after dark. Afterward, enjoy a farewell Budapest dinner at a rooftop restaurant or a modern Hungarian bistro in the city center.

meals.breakfast: Café breakfast near the hotel – Hungarian-style scrambled eggs (tojásrántotta) with bread and coffee (~€7–10)
meals.lunch: Light lunch in the Jewish Quarter – try a Jewish-Hungarian deli or a street food lángos (deep-fried dough with sour cream and cheese) (~€8–12)
meals.dinner: Upscale-casual Hungarian bistro for a farewell dinner – try foie gras Hungarian-style or duck leg with red cabbage (~€22–30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Parliament tours must be booked online in advance at the official website (parlament.hu). Evening Danube cruises depart frequently from Vigadó tér pier – book a reputable operator like Legenda or Mahart PassNave. This is your last full evening in Budapest – savor it!

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a relaxed final morning in Budapest. Visit the Széchenyi Thermal Baths in City Park (Városliget) for a morning soak – one of the largest and most famous thermal bath complexes in Europe (~€22–28 entry). Afterward, stroll through City Park and see the Vajdahunyad Castle and Heroes' Square (Hősök tere), a grand millennium monument.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute souvenir shopping on Váci Street or at the Central Market Hall. Pick up Hungarian paprika, Tokaji wine, Unicum liqueur, or hand-embroidered folk textiles as gifts. Enjoy a final coffee at a traditional Hungarian kávéház (coffeehouse) like Gerbeaud on Vörösmarty Square.
day_by_day.evening: Transfer to Budapest Ferenc Liszt International Airport for your departure flight. Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before departure for check-in and security. Reflect on a wonderful 8-day journey through two of Central Europe's most captivating cities!

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the hotel or a nearby café before heading to the baths (~€6–9)
meals.lunch: Final Hungarian lunch near Váci Street or the Central Market Hall – try a hearty bowl of gulyás soup (~€10–14)
meals.dinner: Airport restaurant or grab a snack before your flight (~€10–15)

day_by_day.notes: Széchenyi Baths open at 06:00 – going early on a weekday means fewer crowds. Book bath entry online to save time. The airport is approximately 30–40 minutes from the city center by taxi (~€25–30) or 40–50 minutes by the 100E airport express bus (~€4). Confirm your flight time and allow ample travel time to the airport.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely start with a gourmet hotel breakfast. At 10:00, begin a private guided walking tour of Prague's UNESCO-listed Old Town. Explore the Astronomical Clock (Orloj) on the hour, wander through Týn Church, and stroll the medieval lanes of Staré Město with expert historical commentary.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross the iconic Charles Bridge with your private guide, pausing at each of the 30 baroque statues for their stories. Ascend to Prague Castle (Pražský hrad) – the largest ancient castle complex in the world. Tour St. Vitus Cathedral, the Old Royal Palace, and the Golden Lane. Enjoy panoramic views over the red-roofed city below.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset aperitivo at Terasa U Zlaté Studně (At the Golden Well) rooftop terrace with sweeping castle views. Dinner at Field Restaurant – one of Prague's most celebrated fine-dining establishments, known for its creative Czech tasting menus with wine pairings sourced from Bohemian and Moravian vineyards.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet hotel breakfast – eggs Benedict, smoked salmon, fresh pastries, seasonal fruit
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Café Savoy – a beautifully restored neo-Renaissance café serving classic Czech open-faced sandwiches (chlebíčky) and artisan coffee
meals.dinner: Field Restaurant – 5-course tasting menu with Czech wine pairing (approx. €120–€150 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes for cobblestoned streets. Castle complex can take 3–4 hours. Book Field Restaurant well in advance through the hotel concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Private morning tour of the Jewish Quarter (Josefov) – one of the best-preserved Jewish quarters in Europe. Visit the Old Jewish Cemetery, the Pinkas Synagogue (Holocaust memorial), and the Spanish Synagogue with its stunning Moorish interior. A knowledgeable guide will bring centuries of history to life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Mucha Museum to explore the Art Nouveau masterpieces of Alfons Mucha. Then, take a private chauffeured drive to the Vinohrady district for an exclusive Czech crystal and Bohemian glass shopping experience at a curated atelier. Alternatively, browse luxury boutiques along Pařížská Street (Prague's answer to the Champs-Élysées).
day_by_day.evening: Attend a private evening performance at the stunning Estates Theatre (Stavovské divadlo) – the very hall where Mozart premiered Don Giovanni in 1787. Pre-show dinner at La Degustation Bohême Bourgeoise, a Michelin-starred restaurant celebrating elevated Czech culinary heritage.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast – continental spread with fresh-pressed juices and local honey
meals.lunch: Lokál Dlouhááá – an upscale Czech gastropub serving perfectly poured Pilsner Urquell and traditional svíčková (beef sirloin in cream sauce) in a lively yet refined atmosphere
meals.dinner: La Degustation Bohême Bourgeoise – 11-course Michelin-starred tasting menu (approx. €130–€160 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Jewish Quarter entry requires tickets – arrange in advance. Estates Theatre performances vary; confirm program with concierge. Dress code for dinner and theatre: smart elegant.

day_by_day.morning: Morning at leisure. Optional: sunrise photography walk along the Vltava riverbanks with a private photographer – capture Charles Bridge and Prague Castle in the golden morning light. Return for a late hotel breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private half-day excursion to Kutná Hora (1.5 hours from Prague) – a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Visit the hauntingly beautiful Sedlec Ossuary (Bone Church), decorated with the bones of 40,000 people, and the magnificent Gothic Cathedral of St. Barbara. Return to Prague by early evening.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Prague evening: sunset cruise on the Vltava River aboard a private boat with champagne and canapés. Dinner at Alcron Restaurant (Radisson Blu Alcron Hotel) – an Art Deco gem offering exceptional seafood and European fine dining in an intimate, glamorous setting.

meals.breakfast: Late hotel breakfast – smoked salmon eggs royale, fresh pastries, specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Packed gourmet picnic prepared by the hotel for the Kutná Hora excursion – local charcuterie, artisan cheeses, Czech bread, sparkling water
meals.dinner: Alcron Restaurant – à la carte fine dining with seasonal European menu and sommelier-selected wine (approx. €100–€130 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Kutná Hora excursion departs by 10:00 AM to allow sufficient time. Private car recommended. Vltava cruise should be booked 48 hours in advance through the hotel concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Private luxury transfer from Prague to Budapest by premium car service or first-class train (Railjet – approx. 7 hours, scenic Danube valley views) or opt for a short private charter flight (approx. 1 hour). Depart by 08:00 to maximize Budapest arrival time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Budapest early-to-mid afternoon. Private luxury transfer to your hotel. Check-in and freshen up. Begin a brief orientation walk along the Danube Promenade (Duna-korzó) with your private Budapest guide, taking in the Parliament Building from across the river and the iconic Chain Bridge.
day_by_day.evening: Welcome dinner in Budapest at Costes Restaurant – Budapest's first and most celebrated Michelin-starred restaurant. Enjoy a contemporary Hungarian tasting menu showcasing seasonal ingredients with an extraordinary wine list featuring Tokaj and Eger selections.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or premium station lounge breakfast in Prague before departure
meals.lunch: First-class train dining car or a curated lunch box prepared by the hotel for the journey
meals.dinner: Costes Restaurant – 7-course tasting menu with Hungarian wine pairing (approx. €110–€140 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Train option is highly scenic and recommended for the experience. Book first-class Railjet tickets in advance. If flying, a private charter from Prague Václav Havel Airport is available. Confirm Budapest hotel arrival time with concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of Buda Castle District – a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Explore the Royal Palace, Matthias Church (Mátyás-templom) with its stunning geometric tiled roof, and the Fisherman's Bastion (Halászbástya) offering breathtaking panoramic views of Pest, the Parliament, and the Danube.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross the legendary Chain Bridge on foot for the atmosphere, then visit the Hungarian Parliament Building (Országház) – one of the most beautiful legislative buildings in the world – on a private guided tour of its gilded interior halls and the Hungarian Holy Crown. Afternoon visit to the Hungarian National Museum for a deep dive into 1,000 years of Magyar history.
day_by_day.evening: Exclusive thermal spa experience at Széchenyi Thermal Bath – reserved for a private evening session (book exclusive hours). Dinner at Onyx Restaurant – a two-Michelin-starred restaurant in the heart of Budapest offering an extraordinary modern Hungarian fine-dining experience.

meals.breakfast: Hotel gourmet breakfast – Hungarian lángos-inspired eggs dish, fresh pastries, cold cuts, seasonal fruit
meals.lunch: Gerbeaud Café on Vörösmarty Square – Budapest's most iconic and elegant coffeehouse, serving Hungarian pastries, cakes, and light lunches since 1858
meals.dinner: Onyx Restaurant – signature tasting menu with wine pairing (approx. €130–€160 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Parliament tour requires advance booking – arrange through concierge. Széchenyi private evening sessions are limited; reserve immediately upon arrival in Budapest. Smart dress required for Onyx.

day_by_day.morning: Private morning boat cruise on the Danube with a local historian guide – glide past Margaret Island, the Parliament Building, Buda Castle, and the Chain Bridge. Enjoy champagne and pastries on board as the city unfolds from the water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the vibrant Great Market Hall (Nagycsarnok) with your guide – Budapest's largest and most atmospheric indoor market. Sample Hungarian specialties: Mangalica sausage, Tokaj wine, paprika varieties, and handmade strudel. Then visit the Great Synagogue on Dohány Street – the largest synagogue in Europe – and the adjacent Jewish Quarter (Erzsébetváros) with its unique ruin bars and Art Nouveau architecture.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at 360 Bar – Budapest's premier rooftop bar atop the Paris Department Store, with 360-degree views of the city skyline. Farewell Budapest dinner at Kollázs Brasserie & Bar (Four Seasons Gresham Palace) – dining inside one of the world's most spectacular Art Nouveau buildings, with refined Hungarian and European cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast – full Hungarian spread with salami, paprika cheese, fresh bread, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Market tasting lunch at the Great Market Hall – charcuterie, lángos, fresh pastries, and a glass of local Tokaj Furmint
meals.dinner: Kollázs Brasserie & Bar, Four Seasons Gresham Palace – à la carte fine dining (approx. €90–€120 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Great Market Hall is closed Sundays – confirmed open on Monday. Gresham Palace is one of the finest Art Nouveau buildings in Europe; even a pre-dinner lobby walk is worthwhile. Book 360 Bar in advance for sunset slot.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely final morning. Late hotel checkout (arrange with concierge in advance). Optional: stroll through Andrássy Avenue – Budapest's grand Champs-Élysées-style boulevard, a UNESCO site – and visit the Hungarian State Opera House exterior or take a brief interior tour if available. Browse luxury boutiques along Váci Street for last-minute gifts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Farewell lunch at a riverside restaurant. Private luxury transfer to Budapest Ferenc Liszt International Airport. Departure.
day_by_day.evening: Departure / In-flight

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast – full gourmet spread, specialty Hungarian coffee, fresh pastries
meals.lunch: Spoon The Boat – an elegant floating restaurant on the Danube serving refined European cuisine with spectacular Parliament views (approx. €50–€70 per person)
meals.dinner: In-flight or at airport lounge

day_by_day.notes: Arrange late checkout (12:00–14:00) with the hotel upon check-in. Confirm departure transfer timing with concierge the evening prior. Allow at least 3 hours before international flight departure. Carry any purchased Tokaj wine or crystal in checked luggage.

query: Eastern Europe city hop Prague + Budapest, $1200, 8 days, September 2026
